record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.context_brief: SUSY GUT proton decay and doublet-triplet splitting
record.original_question: Supersymmetric GUTs contain proton-decay channels beyond ordinary dimension-six gauge-boson exchange, especially dimension-five decay mediated by colored Higgsino triplets that accompany electroweak Higgs doublets in unified multiplets. How can a SUSY GUT keep the color-triplet Higgs states heavy enough to satisfy proton-lifetime bounds such as τ(p → K+ν) above roughly 10^32 years while leaving electroweak Higgs doublets light, and can a natural doublet-triplet splitting mechanism be implemented in a complete model?

evidence.quote: Question #14 Proton decay again: Why doesn’t the proton decay in 10^32 years?
A much more problematic dimension-five contribution arises in supersymmetric GUT’s via mediation by colored Higgsino triplets.
Indeed, in order not to violate current experimental bounds, we must ensure that τ(p → K+ν) > about 10^32 years. This is the problem of ‘doublet-triplet splitting’.
Constructing a fully consistent SO(10) model in which this mechanism is implemented in a natural way remains an active area of research, and many proposals exist.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a supersymmetric grand unified theory (SUSY GUT) based on a simple gauge group G ⊃ SU(3)_c × SU(2)_L × U(1)_Y (for example SU(5) or SO(10)), in which the two MSSM Higgs doublets H_u, H_d are embedded into larger unified Higgs multiplets that necessarily also contain color-triplet partners T, T̄ carrying the quantum numbers of SU(3)_c triplets. Below the unification scale M_GUT ~ 2×10^16 GeV the theory must reduce to the MSSM, so the doublets must remain at the electroweak scale (mass ~ 10^2 GeV) while the triplets must be very heavy.

Proton decay. In such SUSY GUTs the exchange of the color-triplet Higgsinos generates dimension-five operators of the form (QQQL)/M_T and (u^c u^c d^c e^c)/M_T which, dressed by gaugino/Higgsino loops, produce proton-decay amplitudes dominated by the channel p → K^+ ν. The current experimental bound requires τ(p → K^+ ν) ≳ 10^{32} years, which translates into a lower bound on the effective color-triplet mass M_T (typically M_T ≳ 10^{17} GeV after including model-dependent factors).

Problem. 
(a) Construct an explicit, fully consistent renormalizable supersymmetric grand unified model — including a choice of gauge group G, Higgs representation content, superpotential, and vacuum — in which:
  (i) the two electroweak Higgs doublets H_u, H_d remain massless (or with masses of order the electroweak scale) at tree level,
  (ii) their color-triplet partners T, T̄ acquire masses large enough to make τ(p → K^+ ν) > 10^{32} years through the induced dimension-five operators,
  (iii) the splitting in (i)–(ii) is "natural" in the technical sense that it follows from symmetries or from the structure of the superpotential rather than from a tuning of unrelated parameters to a precision finer than ~1%,
  (iv) gauge coupling unification is preserved.

(b) Alternatively, prove that no such natural doublet-triplet splitting mechanism can be realized in a four-dimensional renormalizable SUSY GUT consistent with all current proton-decay bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The doublet-triplet splitting problem in SUSY GUTs remains an active research area. Multiple partial mechanisms exist (missing-partner, Dimopoulos–Wilczek for SO(10), orbifold/extra-dimensional projection, pseudo-Goldstone, dynamical GUT breaking), but no consensus four-dimensional renormalizable model achieves the splitting fully naturally while simultaneously satisfying the latest p → K^+ ν constraints; recent 2024 work continues to propose new constructions and to constrain colored-Higgsino-mediated decay, indicating the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Proton decay in SUSY GUTs
status_evidence.snippet: Review discusses color-triplet Higgsino-mediated dimension-five proton decay and tensions with experimental limits in various SUSY GUT models.
status_evidence.claim: Doublet-triplet splitting and induced p→Kν decay remain central, model-dependent issues in SUSY GUTs.

status_evidence.title: Gauge coupling unification and doublet-triplet splitting via GUT dynamical breaking
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a new mechanism linking gauge coupling unification to doublet-triplet splitting via dynamical GUT breaking.
status_evidence.claim: New mechanisms for doublet-triplet splitting are still being proposed, indicating the problem is not considered solved.

status_evidence.title: Muon g-2 and Proton Lifetime in SUSY SU(5) GUTs with Split Superpartners
status_evidence.snippet: Finds that proton-decay bounds in SUSY SU(5) require effective colored Higgsino Yukawa couplings suppressed by 10^-4–10^-3.
status_evidence.claim: Satisfying proton-decay bounds in SUSY SU(5) still requires substantial model-building input.
